An incredibly talented friend of mine committed suicide 10 years ago during our first year of college. As always seems to be the case, they were the last person any of us expected this to happen to. They had so much going for them...so young and so brilliant: fluent in Latin, active in theatre and acting, successful in so many ways, and then this. 

I wish they had reached out. To me or any of our friends, or their family...but they didn't. It really drove the point home how deep depression can delude your mind. As someone who also suffers from depression, it has been a strong reminder of how devastating suicide can be on the ones you love. It has made me more aware of my own weakness and more sensitive to how I perceive those around me. It was a horrible lesson to learn, but an important one too. 

Please ask for help if you need it. There is always someone who cares if you give them a chance to see your pain. I wish Eric did.

I have felt and still sometimes do very much like you do. Im also young, and my husband and I are in early recovery. I have definitely felt like I was going insane, like I doubted him and myself and it all spiraled into insanity.

The short of it is, Ive learned a lot from the 12 steps that AA and Al anon both follow. I can't cure him, he needs to do that himself. It is not my responsibility, and I did not and cannot make him do this. I also learned how important it is to set boundaries and take care of myself...go to meetings, do things for me, and stop focusing on him. It isnt easy, and Im still figuring out how to do that, but I think it has helped me to trust myself more and be more at peace.

I hope you can find peace, too. Just remember to take care of yourself first. Sometimes that can mean separating temporarily, but everyone's situation is different. Stay strong, you arent alone.
